challenges.title: A non-blocking scheduler and button debounce
challenges.prompt: Implement poll() so each task runs when its period has elapsed using a rollover-safe millis comparison (and no drift), and debounce() so the stable button level flips only after three identical consecutive samples. The program starts near the 32-bit millis() rollover.
challenges.expected:
blink blink sensor blink blink sensor blink report blink sensor blink blink sensor blink blink sensor report blink blink sensor 
runs: blink=12 sensor=6 report=2
sample 6: PRESSED
sample 12: RELEASED
challenges.explain: Comparing with (int32_t)(now - due) >= 0 keeps scheduling correct when millis() wraps after ~49 days, and advancing next_due by the period avoids drift. Counting stable samples filters contact bounce without delay(). Verified by compiling and running the solution with gcc (host-side logic).

challenges.title: Ring buffer, clamped map and ADC divider maths
challenges.prompt: Implement ring_push (overwrite oldest), ring_avg and map_clamped, then use the provided adc_to_volts to convert readings across a 220k/100k divider. Run the readings through the buffer to see how averaging smooths a noisy spike.
challenges.expected:
after 1 samples: count=1 avg=500.0
after 2 samples: count=2 avg=510.0
after 3 samples: count=3 avg=510.0
after 4 samples: count=4 avg=607.5
after 5 samples: count=4 avg=608.8
after 6 samples: count=4 avg=607.5
map 512 -> 50, below range -> 0, above range -> 100
raw 1023 = 3.20 V, raw 512 = 1.60 V
challenges.explain: A fixed-size ring buffer bounds memory, averaging smooths spikes, and clamping before mapping stops out-of-range readings producing out-of-range outputs. Verified by compiling and running the solution with gcc (host-side logic).
